relationships.subject: Insulin
relationships.evidence_quote: We observed that ASIC currents were rapidly enhanced by the preapplication of insulin to rat DRG neurons.

relationships.subject: Insulin receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: These results showed that the enhancement of ASIC currents required the activation of insulin receptors.

relationships.subject: Tyrosine kinase
relationships.evidence_quote: These results indicate that tyrosine kinases were involved in the intracellular signaling pathways that contributed to the insulin-induced enhancement of ASIC currents in DRG neurons.

relationships.subject: PI3 kinase
relationships.evidence_quote: Thus, a PI3 kinase pathway was likely involved in the insulin-induced enhancement of ASIC currents.

relationships.subject: Insulin
relationships.evidence_quote: These results suggested that insulin can dose-dependently increase acid-induced spontaneous nociceptive behaviors through peripheral insulin receptors.

key_findings: Insulin enhances ASIC3-like acid-evoked currents and action potentials in rat DRG neurons via insulin receptor, tyrosine kinase and PI3 kinase
Local insulin exacerbates acid-induced nociceptive behavior and mechanical hyperalgesia through peripheral insulin receptors
